title: Shared edge contracts — every arrow in the graph carries one of these shapes

Provenance.description: Every artifact says who made it and under what method. Required on all top-level contracts.

Surface.description: A thing a change can touch. Used for conflict detection, blast radius, and security scoping.

WorkItem.description: What enters Build. Produced by Project Create (first pass) and Build Re-entry (after launch).

surfaces.description: What this item is expected to touch. Build re-entry's Conflict Detector overlaps on these; without them it is guessing.

patch_ref.description: The Patch JSON this item carries, by ref.

branch.description: An existing change to re-verify rather than re-implement (build-implement verify_only).

Spec.description: Spec Writer output. The single source of truth for Decomposer, Implementer, Test Author, and every Verifier lens.

Task.description: One node in a Task Graph. Owned surfaces must be disjoint across tasks in the same spec.

depends_on.description: Task ids. Only for real data dependencies.

criteria_ids.description: Which acceptance criteria this task satisfies.

ChangeSet.description: Implementer / Fixer / Patch Drafter output. Verifiers receive diff_ref and NOT notes.

diff_ref.description: Pointer to the diff artifact; never inline the diff.

branch.description: Branch the change is committed on. Without it a change set cannot be re-verified later (build-implement verify_only).

ChangeSet.comment: task_id and spec_id are optional: a Patch Drafter's change set (§4) exists before any Task or Spec does, and acquires them when the patch enters Build.

criteria_coverage.description: Acceptance criterion ids this set exercises.

target.description: Which artifact the fix belongs in. Set by the lens; when absent, routing falls back to location (build-implement's routeFinding).

Verdict.description: One lens's opinion. Empty attempts is invalid — the tool layer must reject and retry.

PanelResult.description: Adjudicator output. Pure code; no provenance model field.

Escalation.description: The only thing a Fix Loop shows a human.

Repro.description: Reproducer → Root Cause Analyst (OPERATING_MODEL §4). A named shape because it crosses an edge; Patch.repro is the same thing at rest.

attempts.description: Reproduction attempts spent. Two failures park the signal (§4).

failing_test_ref.description: A test that FAILS on the live behavior. The patch's regression test starts here.

notes.description: What was tried. Feeds the next attempt; never a substitute for a failing test.

PatchVerification.description: Why a Patch may be called verified. Every field is a measurement a mechanical agent took; the verdict is derived from them in script code, never declared by an agent.

repro_at_base.description: The regression test run at base_commit. It MUST fail here, or the patch proves nothing.

Mitigation.description: Mitigator (OPERATING_MODEL §4). The fast reversible action taken on a sev1 BEFORE any human is paged and in parallel with diagnosis. applied=false is a real outcome, never an absent field.

from_sha.description: What the env was serving before.

to_ref.description: The target as given. Resolved, never substituted.

lift_means.description: What the human is deciding when they choose lift_mitigation.

reason.description: Why this strategy, or why nothing was applied.

IncidentRecord.description: Incident Commander (OPERATING_MODEL §4). The sev1 page's payload. Its options depend on whether the mitigation landed: a failed mitigation never offers keep/lift.

ReentryPlan.description: Build re-entry (OPERATING_MODEL §3). The ordered WorkItem[] is the product; this is the why, and it is what the Ratio Gate decides on.

starved_items.description: deferred_iterations >= threshold. Belongs in EvidenceBundle.starved_items downstream.

gate_required.description: Ratio Gate. True only on a breach streak >= 2; the plan is provisional until the human answers.

Patch.description: Maintain → Build re-entry. A ChangeSet plus the why. Never drafted without repro or explicit cannot_repro.

mitigation_id.description: The sev1 mitigation this patch is the real fix for; shipping it is what lets the mitigation be lifted.

EvidenceBundle.description: Build → Launch. Everything a human needs to veto, and nothing they don't.

integration_commit.description: The sha the Integrator produced. artifact_ref is a branch name, which dies with its container; this is the only durable handle on what a run shipped. Company Memory's Lens Calibrator joins Cause.suspect_commit to this field to find the PanelResult that passed a defect. Optional: nothing stamps it yet.

tests_landed.description: TestSet files the Integrator copied into the repo's test directory and committed. A TestSet that stays in the artifact store is run once and lost, so the suite never grows and defects escape through behavior nothing tests; this records which tests actually entered the repo.

tests_skipped.description: TestSet files NOT landed because a file of that name already existed. Reported, never overwritten.

spec_refs.description: Paths to the full Spec JSON of each shipped spec. Launch's Release Notes Writer reads these; ids alone carry no content.

migrations.description: Schema migrations the candidate carries. Absent = Build did not declare; Preflight then scans the diff itself and never assumes none.

ProjectBrief.description: Scope & Contract output. For self-owned ventures the founder is both HE and HC; the shape does not change.

hosting.description: Where the Env Provisioner puts the environments. Without it Project Create cannot provision and refuses; nothing defaults.

app_dir.description: Repository-relative directory of the deployable app (e.g. toy).

envs.description: env name → port. Launch needs prod and canary.

Workspace.description: Project Create output. Handles only — every node re-reads what it needs.

comms.description: client channel, status page, review queue

Signal.description: Normalized input to Maintain. Produced by code from telemetry, alerts, error trackers, and user reports.

facts.description: The observations severity is DERIVED from. §4's Severity Router is code: the agent reports what it sees, the script decides the severity, and this is the record of why.

data_at_risk.description: Stored data is being lost, corrupted or exposed.

severity_rule.description: The code rule that turned facts into severity.

HealthReport.description: Maintain → Improve / Evidence / Memory. Rolled up by code on a cadence.

patches_drafted.description: Drafted by Maintain this period. patches_shipped is Build's number, not Maintain's.

parked_signals.description: cannot_repro after the attempt cap: the holding set (§4).

maintain_ratio.description: Share of Build capacity consumed by maintain work.

maintain_ratio_source.description: Maintain never sees Build capacity or the improve backlog, so this number is provisional unless Build re-entry supplied it.

trend_basis.description: What the trend was derived from. A trend with no prior period is not a trend.

FeedbackItem.description: Improve input. One normalized item off a client channel, review, or support queue. The Feedback Collector is code (OPERATING_MODEL 5.1): it reads and shapes, it does not judge. Persisted, so it is a def rather than an inline schema.

asks_for.description: What the sender wants, in their terms. The Feedback Analyst themes these; it never invents an ask.

TelemetrySnapshot.description: Improve input. Usage over one period. Signal is Maintain's alert shape (one fingerprinted fault); this is the aggregate the Usage Analyst reads against ProjectBrief.success_metrics. Deliberately loose under line/http: the Analyst is what turns raw counters into insights, so a schema that pinned every counter would move that judgment into the contract.

line.description: What the production line did: launches, human actions by stretch, cost by workflow. For a venture whose stated users are the plant itself, this IS the usage.

http.description: What the service underneath served: requests by route, error rates, parameter usage.

MemoryRoll.description: Company Memory output (OPERATING_MODEL 8), one artifact per roll. Five outputs in one def rather than five defs: they are read together and they are written together. Dark Factory sink; nothing waits on it.

runs_read.description: run_ids this roll is computed from. A roll that names no runs is asserting nothing.

patterns.description: Pattern Extractor. Every claim carries the runs it came from and how many; a pattern with sample_size 1 is a note, not a pattern, and says so.

calibration.description: Estimate Calibrator. basis is run_level until the runtime exposes per-agent tokens and a script stamps Provenance.tokens; node_level calibration is not available today and must not be claimed.

lens_catch_rates.description: Lens Calibrator. catch_rate is null, with unavailable_reason set, whenever the denominator does not exist: a rate needs defects that PASSED a panel and were later found by Maintain. Defects planted by hand on a branch no panel ever saw are not lens misses and are never counted as any. Null is the honest answer; a fabricated percentage is not.

mutation.description: Passed verbatim as build-implement's canary.mutation arg.

origin.description: Where this defect was really seen: a run_id, a signal id, or 'synthetic'.

expected_lens.description: Which lens SHOULD catch it. A canary no lens is expected to catch measures nothing.

canaries.description: Canary Injector's library. build-implement's existing canary arg consumes mutation directly.

outcomes.description: Counted outcomes per method. LedgerEntry records status and escalations only, so shipped / vetoed / came-back-as-a-defect are not available until something records them; keys absent means not measured, never zero.

method_report.description: The Method Ledger report: provenance.method x outcome x cost. The question the whole model exists to answer.

review_queue.description: HOTL, not HITL: prompts flagged for a human to look at (a lens that passed a canary, 2.4.4). Lands in a queue; nothing waits on it. There is no review-queue substrate yet - gates/ is HITL only - so this is carried in the roll.

Opportunity.description: Improve internal. Synthesized from usage insights + feedback themes; ranked by code.

surfaces.description: What this opportunity would touch. Build re-entry's Conflict Detector overlaps on WorkItem.surfaces; without this the Backlog Emitter has nothing to carry over and re-entry pays a cheap agent to guess them.

score.description: Prioritizer output, DERIVED IN SCRIPT CODE: expected_value x confidence / cost. Never an agent's number.

within_budget.description: Whether this fell inside the remaining budget when the Prioritizer cut the list. Array order cannot record where the cut fell; this can.

VentureVerdict.description: Improve → HE. Periodic recommendation on a self-owned venture. The human decides; this is the evidence.

measured.description: Whether the period's telemetry measured this metric at all, and whether its target parses as a comparison. An UNMEASURED metric is neither met nor missed; met is false for it because a missing measurement must never satisfy a success metric, but false alone cannot say which of the two it is. Without this field a verdict reads "2 of 3 met" when the third was never looked at.

ReviewPackage.description: Launch → Approval Gate. The one page the HC reads before approve / veto. Assembled by code from Preflight, the Release Notes Writer and the EvidenceBundle digest.

artifact_sha.description: The commit Preflight pinned. A branch name can move; the sha is what gets deployed.

release_notes.description: Short, inlined: the package is one page.

open_gates.description: Open gate ids for this project at preflight time (sev1 pages, escalations).

options.description: approve only appears when preflight.go; a no-go offers veto or approve_override (a note is mandatory and lands in the LaunchRecord).

Deployment.description: Deployer → Post-launch Watch → Recorder. One environment running one pinned sha. Written by substrate/deploy.js.

WatchReport.description: Post-launch Watch → Recorder. Canary vs baseline over the window, round by round; the verdict is derived by the workflow script from the thresholds, never declared by an agent.

override_reason.description: Present only when the HC chose approve_override on a no-go preflight.

live_url.description: The Live Product handle: what prod serves after this launch (the candidate if healthy, the baseline if rolled back).

seeded_regression.description: Test-only. The mutation applied to the canary before the watch, so a rollback drill is never mistaken for a real one.

GateRecord.description: Substrate. A workflow output that needs a human decision, written to gates/ by the main session at a workflow boundary. The human's decision is recorded here and carried into the next workflow's args.

gate.description: Gate name from the operating model, e.g. brief_approval, spec_gate, launch_approval, sev1_page, roadmap_gate, venture_verdict, ratio_gate, escalation, portfolio_gate, machine_release_gate.

workflow.description: The workflow whose return opened this gate.

next_workflow.description: The workflow that consumes the decision.

selection.description: Ids the human picked when the decision is more than one word - e.g. the approved Opportunity ids at the roadmap_gate, where decision.option carries the VentureVerdict recommendation. Structured, so the next workflow reads a list instead of parsing note.

LedgerEntry.description: Substrate. One row per workflow run in ledger/. Tokens and wall clock are stamped after the run returns because the script can see neither; this is the Method Ledger's unit of account.

tokens_by_model.description: Runtime token count per model id. Tokens are not comparable across tiers; this is what the Method Ledger prices.

cost_est_usd.description: Estimated cost from substrate/lib/pricing.json (blended per-model rate; see its note).

artifact_count.description: Nested objects carrying provenance in the stored result.

trace_ref.description: Copy of the runtime journal, by ref.

wall_clock_unknown.description: The recorded wall clock is known to be wrong and is excluded from aggregates; tokens and cost remain valid.
